run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T03:11:08Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error spans on frontend-proxy itself: ingress spans with http.status_code 500 (around 03:13-03:17) and 504/503 (around 03:19-03:27), peaking at a 10-minute error-span rate of 1.398/s at 03:21:08 versus 0.0035-0.0105/s before 03:12 (evidence 479542ec-ffce-4f1c-9810-1fccbac278be-t1:4c4b9a37-8c58-46f4-8556-86d9ae68818e, eb22621a-53b3-4389-b613-4370a841358a-t1:2cd4bb94-a1d4-4149-8b78-03f6a55af120). The failures trace to the ad service: the ad Deployment was restarted at 03:12:28 (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation, new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5, old ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 scaled to 0, old pod deleted), and the replacement pod has no readiness/liveness/startup probe at all while carrying a 50m CPU limit. Frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds calls first failed with '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' (the ad Service ClusterIP) at 03:14:58 and still at 03:16:57-03:16:59, producing frontend 500s and frontend-proxy 500s; then, once the new pod was answering, ad GetAds p90 latency rose from a 50-150 ms baseline to 380-1052 ms, its client spans to flagd (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean) took 0.69-4.4 s with grpc status 4 while flagd's own server spans stayed at 49-112 us, and frontend /api/data calls took 10.8-19.7 s, exceeding frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout and yielding 504s. The new ad container's CPU usage was 0.035-0.049 cores with 92-100% of CFS periods throttled, versus 0.005-0.009 cores and 8-32% throttling for the pod that ran before the restart; throttling and ad latency both fell back after ~03:24-03:28. Flagd, the Service/Endpoints configuration, and the frontend pod were checked and are not supported as causes. One part remains unresolved: the alert's stated start 03:11:08 precedes the ad restart by ~80 s, and a low-rate frontend-proxy 503 pattern existed already from 02:57, so the first reason the rule satisfied 'above 0' cannot be pinned to the ad restart alone; the alerting rule itself was not exposed by Prometheus.

claims.text: frontend-proxy emitted its own error spans in the incident window: 10-minute error span rate rose from 0 at 02:51/02:54 and 0.0035-0.0105/s at 02:57-03:12 to 0.384/s at 03:15:08, 0.975/s at 03:18:08, 1.398/s at 03:21:08, 1.212/s at 03:24:08, 0.653/s at 03:27:08 and 0.084/s at 03:30:08.

frontend-proxy ingress spans carried http.status_code 500 and 504 with otel.status_code ERROR, and its 'router frontend egress' client spans to the frontend service carried error=true with http.status_code 0 (no response); the 504 spans lasted about 15.0 s.

At 03:11:08, before the ad restart, frontend-proxy already had a nonzero but small error span rate: ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.0105/s vs 11.92/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.

Sampled frontend-proxy errors from 03:06:32 to 03:11:30 (before the ad restart) are ingress 503s on load-generator GETs whose 'router frontend egress' span failed with http.status_code 0, for which the sampled traces contain no frontend server span.

The frontend service's own spans show the failing dependency: at 03:20:00 grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds had STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.654/s and GET /api/data and GET had the same 0.654/s error rate, while cart, checkout, recommendation and product-catalog calls showed no errors.

frontend spans record the exact diagnostic text '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (rpc.grpc.status_code=14, otel.status_code=ERROR) at 03:14:58 and again at 03:16:57-03:16:59, propagating as 500s on GET /api/data, frontend GET, frontend-proxy ingress and load-generator GET.

The address in that error is the ad Service ClusterIP: service ad is ClusterIP 100.70.197.56 with port 8080 and targetPort 8080 selecting opentelemetry.io/name=ad, and its Endpoints object lists exactly one address, pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh at 100.96.3.224 port 8080.

The ad Deployment was rolled out/restarted at 03:12:28: annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T03:12:28Z, deployment revision 2, events show SuccessfulCreate of pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh (Scheduled 03:12:28, Created 03:12:29, Started 03:12:30) and SuccessfulDelete of pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc (Killing 03:12:30); ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 now has 1 replica and ad-554b849958 has 0.

The restart changed no visible container configuration: ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and ad-785b4464f5 both specify image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, containerPort 8080, env AD_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, and resources limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi with requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi; the only template difference is the restartedAt annotation.

The ad container has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe, so a freshly started container is reported ready and is added to the Service endpoints (Endpoints shows it as the only backend) without any check that port 8080 is listening.

The replacement ad pod was CPU-starved: container=ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh had CFS throttling ratios of 0.924 (03:13:08), 0.981 (03:16:08), 1.0 (03:19:08), 0.880 (03:22:08), 0.396 (03:25:08) and 0.285 (03:28:08), versus 0.319-0.081 for the pre-restart pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc; its CPU usage was 0.0353-0.0492 cores versus 0.0012-0.0087 cores for the old pod, against a 50m (0.05 core) limit.

ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server-span p90 duration rose from a 50.3-151.5 ms baseline (02:52:08-03:16:08) to 380 ms (03:18:08), 1052 ms (03:22:08), 592 ms (03:24:08), 445 ms (03:26:08) and fell back to 181-212 ms at 03:28:08-03:30:08.

In traces from 03:19:54 onward, frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans lasted 10.8-19.7 s, the ad server's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans lasted 7.2-19.4 s, ad's own flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean client spans lasted 0.69-4.4 s with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (recorded ERROR), while flagd's server-side ResolveBoolean spans in the same traces lasted 49-112 us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 (one 59 us span carried 'context deadline exceeded', code 2).

During the same period the load-generator's GET spans ended as 504 after ~15.0 s and 500 after 5-6 s, and the ad pod's current log stream shows it serving 'Targeted ad request received' / 'Non-targeted ad request received' lines normally at 03:22-03:23 with no error lines.

flagd showed no resource-side stress of its own: container flagd in pod flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr had CFS throttling ratio 0 at every sampled point from 02:52:08 to 03:28:08, and the flagd pod (started 02:42:14) has 0 restarts with both containers ready.

ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination reason, podIP 100.96.3.224, owned by ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5; frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw and frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-kxdcl are also Running/Ready with 0 restarts.
frontend-proxy and frontend containers were not resource-starved: container frontend-proxy throttling ratio stayed 0.029-0.053 and container frontend 0.261-0.316 across 02:52:08-03:28:08.

Primary supported cause: the ad Deployment restart at 03:12:28 replaced a long-running ad JVM with a cold pod that (a) had no readiness probe, so it entered the ad Service endpoints while its port 8080 was not yet accepting connections - giving frontend 'connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' and 500s at the frontend-proxy - and (b) ran at 92-100% CFS throttling under its 50m CPU limit, making ad's GetAds handling and its flagd ResolveBoolean calls take seconds, so frontend /api/data took 10.8-19.7 s and frontend-proxy returned 504 at its 15 s timeout. Throttling and latency both subsided after ~03:24-03:28 as the error rate fell (0.653/s at 03:27:08, 0.084/s at 03:30:08).

Open second candidate (unresolved): a low-rate frontend-proxy failure already existed before the ad restart - ingress 503s at 0.0035-0.0105/s from 02:57:08 to 03:12:08 whose 'router frontend egress' span failed with http.status_code 0 and whose sampled traces contain no frontend server span - and since the alert is reported as firing since 03:11:08 (before the 03:12:28 restart), that pre-existing condition may be what first pushed RequestErrorRate above 0. Its cause is not established here; it accounts for about 0.01/s, far less than the 1.4/s peak.

flagd as the root cause is not supported: while ad's client spans to flagd took 0.69-4.4 s and expired with grpc status 4, flagd's own server spans in the same traces completed in 49-112 us and flagd had zero CPU throttling and no restarts, so the delay is on the CPU-throttled ad side rather than in flagd's processing.

A Service/Endpoints selector or port misconfiguration for ad is contradicted by the evidence: service ad selects opentelemetry.io/name=ad, the pod carries that label plus pod-template-hash 785b4464f5, targetPort 8080 equals the container port, and Endpoints lists only that pod's IP at port 8080.

The ad pod did not crash: it is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and no terminated last state, and its logs show it answering ad requests normally at 03:22-03:23, so the ad-side problem is unavailability during cold start plus sustained CPU throttling, not a container failure or eviction.

No other service shows a comparable error contribution: the per-service 10-minute error-span rate series returned were accounting and payment at 0, ad 0.0018/s only at 03:06-03:15, fraud-detection 0.0018/s at 03:12-03:21, recommendation a flat ~0.0018/s, against frontend 2.749/s and frontend-proxy 1.398/s at 03:21:08; sampled failing traces contain only frontend-proxy, frontend, ad, flagd and load-generator spans.

One unrelated workload state change was observed: pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 is Running with restartCount 1 and lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled (exitCode 137), and it appears in no failing trace chain; its error-span rate stayed at 0.0018/s or 0.

Give the ad container a real readiness (and startup) probe on gRPC port 8080 so the pod is not added to the ad Service endpoints before it listens, and raise or remove the 50m CPU limit (10m request) so a cold JVM start and steady-state flag evaluation are not throttled at 92-100% of periods; also avoid restarting ad at a time when any 5xx is alerting.

gaps: Prometheus returned no alerting or recording rules (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate, with type=alert and unfiltered all returned no_data), so the exact RequestErrorRate expression, its denominator and the annotation value 'current: 2.4555555555555553' could not be verified, and the reported alert start 03:11:08 precedes the ad restart at 03:12:28 by about 80 s.

The frontend container produced no retrievable log lines in 03:10-03:18 (0 lines read), and the ad container's retained log stream only contains lines from 03:22:18 onward, so the exact moment the new ad process began listening on 8080 and its startup messages could not be read.

flagd, kafka and postgresql are absent from traces_span_metrics_calls_total service_name values, so their latency is only observable through the sampled traces returned, not through a complete metric series.

What the 03:12:28 restartedAt rollout was meant to change is unknown: both ad ReplicaSets advertise identical container specs and the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the reason for the restart cannot be established.
Whether the new ad pod's slow start was caused solely by CPU throttling or also by JVM/agent initialization could not be separated; the ad JVM startup sequence is not directly observable here.

The pre-existing low-rate frontend-proxy 503 pattern (router frontend egress failing with http.status_code 0 and no frontend server span, 02:57-03:12) remains unexplained; it needs frontend-side connection logs or Envoy reset metrics that are not available in this target.
next_steps: Add a gRPC readiness probe on port 8080 and a startupProbe to the ad Deployment, and raise its CPU limit above 50m; verify that a rolling restart no longer leaves the Service with an unlistening backend.

Inspect the ad JVM startup timeline (container start to first accepted connection) on the next restart, e.g. with a temporary startup log line or apiserver-side timing, to confirm how much of the ~5 minute connection-refused window is CPU throttling.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition and its evaluation window from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule configuration (not exposed by this Prometheus) to reconcile the reported 2.4555 value and the 03:11:08 start with the observed error spans.

Investigate the chronic frontend-proxy -> frontend 503 pattern separately, looking at Envoy upstream reset/connect-failure statistics and frontend server connection handling, which were not available in this Run.
